rationale: Tests recall of the most common positioning-related nerve injury, directly addressed in the anatomy and classification content block.
Checks understanding of risk stratification for positioning injuries, emphasising that duration and physiological state both contribute to hazard.
Applies knowledge of the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist as a structured tool for perioperative hazard prevention, covered in the management strategies block.
Tests foundational recall that communication failures are implicated in the majority of sentinel events, establishing the importance of the content block.
Distinguishes errors of execution (slips/lapses) from errors of planning (mistakes), a key conceptual distinction in the classification block.
Applies knowledge of the most effective individual-level prevention strategy for drug errors in anaesthesia — the read-back technique — covered in the prevention strategies block.
